issue.title: Decide whether SASE must disable or reconcile Muse's cron_* tools and per-session cron.db
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-ha.4 (epic sase-ha, Meta Muse Code provider) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP; not covered by the epic plan (sase/repos/plans/202608/muse_provider.md), so it is new work rather than unfinished epic work.

WHAT WAS OBSERVED: while implementing Muse tool-call parsing against the recorded R708.1 fixtures and a live authenticated run, the Muse CLI was seen to expose 'cron_*' tools and to keep a per-session 'cron.db'. It is not known whether a Muse agent can use them to schedule work that keeps running after the 'muse exec' process SASE launched has exited.

WHY IT MATTERS: SASE's contract is that an agent's effects end when its invocation ends. If a Muse agent can register a cron entry that outlives the invocation, SASE would be leaking background work it does not track, cannot show in ACE, and cannot kill — and the epic already had to add MUSE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 (src/sase/llm_provider/muse.py) for the analogous problem of the launcher swapping its own binary mid-run.

SCOPE: determine empirically whether cron_* entries survive process exit and where cron.db lives relative to the SASE-named --session-id; then decide and implement one of (a) leave as-is with a documented note in docs/llms.md, (b) disable the tools for SASE-launched runs if Muse offers a switch, or (c) reconcile/clean the session's cron.db on run teardown. Investigation first; the remediation is expected to be small once the answer is known.

Filed by epic land agent sase-ha.land on 2026-08-08 while landing epic sase-ha.
